subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Elephant in the room

options.text: An obvious issue left unaddressed due to its sensitivity
An extremely fat person sitting all alone in a room
A wild untamed animal left to wander astray
A pretty affair which is kept a secret

solution:
The correct answer is: **An obvious issue left unaddressed due to its sensitivity**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "**Elephant in the room**" means that there is an obvious problem or difficult situation that people do not want to talk about.

 
 
• Example - *We all sat sipping our tea quietly, no one wanting to bring up the **elephant in the room** about Joel's expulsion from the college.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom "**Elephant in the room**" is **"An obvious issue left unaddressed due to its sensitivity"**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
